skills.title: Skills & Agents
skills.subtitle: Everything the agent can use, loaded live from OpenCode.

install.placeholder: Paste a SKILL.md, or a URL / description for the agent to turn into one
install.hintConnected: A pasted SKILL.md installs straight away; anything else opens an agent session. Installed skills are available in every workspace.
install.agentPrompt:
The user typed this into the Skills install box:

---
{{input}}
---

Please help them install it patiently: work out which skill they mean (fetch the URL, search for it, or ask them if it is ambiguous), then save it as a skill file at .opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md inside this workspace — never outside it; the app then makes it available in every workspace. The customize-opencode skill documents the format. Finally reply with the installed skill's name.
install.echo:
Please help me install this skill:

{{input}}
install.adoptFailed: The skill was written but could not be moved into your profile, so it will disappear when this session's folder is replaced: {{detail}}

environment.detectionUnavailable: Environment detection runs in the desktop app.
environment.note: OpenCode runs code with whatever is installed here (e.g. Python via its shell tool). uv ships with the app, and Jupyter can be app-managed in Settings → Connectors. Python and R are not bundled — install them or a Science Pack to enable analysis.

specialists.heading: Specialists
specialists.hint: Your own subagents. The main agent hands them work that matches their description.
specialists.emptyBody: A specialist is a focused helper with its own instructions, limited to the skills and connectors you choose — for example a statistics reviewer that only uses your R skills.
specialists.name: Name
specialists.idHint: Saved as a short ID made from the name.
specialists.whenToUseHint: The main agent reads this to decide when to hand work over. Name the task and the situation.
specialists.whenToUsePlaceholder: e.g. Reviews statistical analyses in R or Python: test choice, assumptions, multiple comparisons.
specialists.whenToUseRequired: Describe when it should be used.
specialists.instructionsHint: Replaces the default system prompt for this specialist. Project memory and the skill list are still included. Leave empty to keep the default.
specialists.instructionsPlaceholder: How it should work, what to check, how to report back.
specialists.capabilitiesHint: What it may use. Approval rules still apply to everything it runs.
specialists.skillsNone: None selected: this specialist uses no skills.
specialists.connectorsHint: Connectors added later are on until you turn them off here.
specialists.noConnectors: No connectors configured. Add them in Settings › Connectors.
specialists.connectorCollision: Turning off {{blocked}} would also turn off {{other}}. Turn both off, or keep {{blocked}} on.
specialists.deleteBody: The main agent will no longer be able to hand work to it. Past sessions keep what it did.
specialists.discardBody: What you changed in this specialist will be lost.
specialists.created: Created {{id}}. The main agent can hand work to it now.
specialists.idEmpty: The name needs at least one letter or digit — it becomes the ID.

detail.empty: This SKILL.md has no instructions beyond its description.
